newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO IN TALKS TO SELL MEESPIERSON.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO IN TALKS TO SELL MEESPIERSON.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Tuesday it was holding discussions about the possible sale of its MeesPierson investment banking unit.
ABN AMRO said it had been approached by a number of parties interested in acquiring MeesPierson and that this coincided with a "broader review of the strategic options of MeesPierson NV".
"As a result ABN AMRO Bank is currently in discussion and will make further announcements if developments so require," it said in a brief statement.

MeesPierson was formed through a 1993 merger of Mees & Hope and Pierson Heldring & Pierson, the Dutch investment banking units of Algemene Bank Nederland (ABN) and Amsterdam-Rotterdam Bank (AMRO) which themselves merged in 1991 to form ABN AMRO.
There has long been speculation that ABN AMRO would divest MeesPierson. This intensified after ABN AMRO acquired London-based securities house Hoare Govett in 1992.
